literal: The beauty and charm of one who does not have subtle, excellent, penetrating intellect is like a well-made, adorned clay doll.
translation: The physical beauty and charm of a person who lacks a subtle, deep, and penetrating intellect is like a beautifully adorned doll made of clay.
modern: நுட்பமான, சிறந்த, ஊடுருவி அறியும் அறிவு இல்லாதவனுடைய அழகும் கவர்ச்சியும், மண்ணால் செய்யப்பட்டு அழகாக அலங்கரிக்கப்பட்ட பொம்மையைப் போன்றதாகும்.
explanation: This couplet compares an unlearned person who lacks deep, penetrating intellect to a beautifully crafted clay doll. Although the clay doll is painted and decorated to look attractive, it lacks life, movement, and real utility. Similarly, a person may possess great physical beauty and charm, but without the inner light of subtle, sharp knowledge, that beauty is superficial and useless. The poet uses the contrast between the external beauty of the doll and its lifeless clay substance to emphasize that true human worth comes from learning and intellect, not physical appearance.
